name: Turnquill Flipbook
author: theconcreteprotector

sections.description:
Publish magazines, catalogues, brochures, and other documents as flipbooks. Upload a PDF or arrange images from the Media Library, then add the flipbook to a WordPress page or embed it on another site.

  • Runs entirely on your own site. There is no account, external service, upsell, or paid version.
  • Display the reader inline or open it from a cover in a dialog. Each flipbook also has its own page.
  • Turn pages with a swipe, drag, keyboard, or buttons. Readers can zoom, browse thumbnails, and share a link to a specific page.
  • Read in single-page or two-page layout, including right-to-left reading order. The reader respects the device’s reduced-motion setting.
  • Search text PDFs, follow embedded links and bookmarks, and open password-protected PDFs. Print and download controls are available for PDFs.
  • Set branding, accent colour, and theme site-wide or per flipbook.
  • Add links, page jumps, or videos to regions of image pages. Image pages use their Media Library alt text.

Privacy

Turnquill bundles the reader and PDF engine and runs without an external service or account. The visitor’s browser may contact another host if you configure externally hosted media or a visitor follows an external link. Videos assigned to image regions load when the visitor plays them.

View counting is off by default. Enable it under Flipbooks > Settings > Privacy. When enabled, the site stores a visit total for each flipbook and uses a salted hash of the visitor’s IP address and browser information for up to 30 minutes to deduplicate opens. The counter sets no cookies. Suggested policy wording is available under Settings > Privacy.

Source Code and Credits

The release includes the compiled reader, TypeScript source, and build instructions in dev/README.md. Installation and use only require WordPress and PHP.

Turnquill source and original artwork are licensed under GPL-2.0-or-later. The combined distribution uses GPL version 3 for compatibility with Apache-2.0 PDF.js. See LICENSE and LICENSE-GPL-3.0.

The bundled PDF.js runtime is from Mozilla’s PDF.js 6.5.438 release. View its source and build tools at https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/tree/v6.5.438. Upstream notices for the engine, fonts, CMaps, colour profiles, and decoders are included in assets/viewer/pdfjs/.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New and install Turnquill, or upload the release ZIP using Upload Plugin. Activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Flipbooks > Add New, choose a PDF or page images from the Media Library, and publish.
  3. Add the Flipbook block to a page and select your publication. You can also copy the shortcode or iframe from the flipbook editor’s Embed box.
  4. Set site-wide branding and display defaults under Flipbooks > Settings.
sections.faq:
How do I use the shortcode?

Use [turnquill id="12"] or select a publication by slug with [turnquill slug="spring-catalogue"]. Add page="4" to set the starting page, height="640px" to set the height, or class="catalogue" to add a CSS class. Use mode="lightbox" to open the reader from a button that uses the featured image as the cover when one is set.

Why can’t readers search my PDF?

Search needs a text layer. Run scanned documents through OCR before uploading. Image flipbooks have no full-text search.

How do I add links or videos to image pages?

In the Display box, use the Links and videos on pages field. Enter JSON keyed by zero-based page index. Each region needs a rect with left, top, width, and height expressed as fractions of the page. Add one action using url, video (a direct file URL), or page (a zero-based destination). Add a descriptive name for the accessible control label.

{"0":[{"rect":[0.1,0.1,0.3,0.2],"url":"https://example.com","name":"Visit the catalogue site"}]}

Who can manage flipbooks?

Administrators and editors receive flipbook capabilities when the plugin is activated. Site administrators can grant those capabilities to other roles.

Are my files private?

Flipbook visibility and passwords control access to the flipbook page. Anyone with a Media Library file’s public URL can still request that file. Use server-level access controls for confidential files. The download setting controls the visibility of the reader’s download button.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

Turnquill removes its settings and capabilities. Flipbook posts, their metadata, and uploaded media remain available when you reinstall.
sections.changelog:
0.3.1

  • New plugin name: Turnquill Flipbook. Text domain and identifiers now use the turnquill prefix.

0.3.0

  • Translate the reader interface and add video regions to image pages.
  • Make view counting opt-in and supply suggested privacy policy text.
  • Preserve image alt text, hotspots, and page jumps when an image attachment is missing.
  • Remove plugin capabilities across multisite when uninstalling.
  • Remove the experimental JSON importer and include the viewer source in the release.

0.2.3

  • Add directory assets and improve escaping and request sanitization.

0.2.2

  • Include the GPL license and retain third-party notices.

0.2.1

  • Improve toolbar layout and navigation contrast on phones.

0.2.0

  • Improve keyboard and dialog navigation, add standalone flipbook pages, and show publication details in the block editor.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
